item.title: Senate rejects resolution to block Trump from striking Iran
item.summary: The war powers resolution was the fourth to fail in the chamber since the war’s start — but some Republicans expressed fresh concern about the war as it approaches the two-month mark.

item.title: Top CDC director pick Erica Schwartz tests White House political balancing act
item.summary: Schwartz would be Trump’s third nominee to lead the agency. The administration is also said to be looking at three other people to serve in senior roles supporting her.

item.title: Trump adviser Sebastian Gorka seeks top counterterrorism job
item.summary: The maneuvering comes a month after Joe Kent, the National Counterterrorism Center’s previous director, resigned in protest over the Iran war.

item.title: Trump says China has agreed not to send weapons to Iran
item.summary: The president made the claim, which Beijing has yet to confirm, amid anger in China that its vessels could be caught up in a U.S. blockade targeting Iranian ports.

item.title: U.S. sends thousands more troops to Mideast as Trump seeks to squeeze Iran
item.summary: The deployment includes sailors and Marines due to arrive as the administration attempts to enforce a maritime blockade against the regime in Tehran.

item.title: Trump says Iran talks may resume this week, but opposes enrichment compromise
item.summary: The lead U.S. negotiator, Vice President JD Vance, has sought a moratorium on uranium enrichment of at least 20 years. Tehran’s offer would last up to five.

item.title: White House touts refunds, as most Americans say taxes are too high
item.summary: The president hopes voters will focus on the benefit of “No Tax on Tips” and other breaks, but economists say higher gas prices will negate most of those benefits.

item.title: Tracking who Trump is appointing to fill key administration roles
item.summary: Follow President Trump’s progress filling over 800 positions, among about 1,300 that require Senate confirmation, in this tracker from The Washington Post and the Partnership for Public Service.

item.title: What Swalwell’s exit means for Democrats in California’s governor race
item.summary: Billionaire Tom Steyer and ex-congresswoman Katie Porter stand to benefit the most in a Democratic field with no clear front-runner, several strategists said.

item.title: DOJ accuses Biden administration of weaponizing abortion access law
item.summary: A long-awaited report from the Justice Department’s “Weaponization Working Group” alleges misuse of the Face Act. But the evidence is limited, and the Trump administration has itself been criticized for misusing law enforcement.
